# BOOK 1: The Chevalier's Daughter; or, An Exile for the Truth (Guernsey, 1660s Normandy/Cornwall/Huguenot exile)

## Frame and setup
- Memoirs of Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin ("Vevette"), written late in life; transcribed by Rosamond Genevieve Corbet, Tre Madoc Court, May 1, 1740. Grandparents' papers found in carved cabinet.
- Born 1660 at Tour d'Antin, near Sartilly, Normandy. Father: Chevalier Armand d'Antin (younger son of De Fayrolles family of Provence, Huguenot). Mother: Margaret (Marguerite) Corbet, English, of Cornish Corbets; pale, grave, devout; called "Pearl" by father.
- Tour d'Antin: reddish stone, square tower (mother's rooms), round tower (ruinous, "white chevalier" ghost legend of wife buried alive), Gothic chapel, Protestant "Temple" at garden end. Views of Mont St. Michel, the Grève (quicksands), All Souls' mist.
- Huguenot persecution background: Edict of Nantes 1598, revoked 1685; Merindol/Cabrières massacres; uncle (family head) converted to curry favor with Louis XIV, family disgrace.

## Early childhood (Ch. I)
- Infant Vevette fostered by Jeanne Sablot (ex-cook, Vaudois ancestry) and husband Simon Sablot (tall, blue-eyed, devout). Children David (older, ~14 later; becomes ship-carpenter at Dieppe) and Lucille ("Loulou," jealous older girl, ~3 years older than Vevette).
- Farm details: brass pans, bahut (carved cabinet with steel hinges, doves and olive-leaf-in-circle maker's mark, made by Jeanne's great-grandfather), sarrasin cakes.
- Psalms of Marot; "Noble Lesson" Vaudois.
- David runs off to Granville St. Michael procession; Vevette tells; Simon warns Vevette never to enter church/kiss image. Vevette calls Lucille "only a little girl" retort. David returned (Vevette kept him from procession).
- Old curé Father Francois (fat, kind, snuff); asks eggs; warns "wolves on road to Sartilly" (a convent/hospital opened at Sartilly, St. Jacques, with Dominican confessor).

## Youth (Ch. II–III)
- Vevette returns to Tour d'Antin at ten (per text; Ch. II). Room in turret off mother's room. Mistress Grace (Cornish, tall, thin, lady's attendant, "Mrs. Grace"; Vevette calls her Gracy). Spinning wheel gift from David (carved; David's uncle blacksmith at Sartilly).
- Reads "Whole Duty of Man," "Practice of Piety," Taylor's "Holy Living and Dying." Steals a stage play (witty, profane), lies; mother punishes. Also hid Sidney's Arcadia and Spenser's Faerie Queene (mother confiscated). Hakluyt's Voyages.
- Hospital of St. Jacques fever/fire/flood; nuns leave.
- Persecution narrative (galleys, convents, pastors). Father's estate ethics (steward under God).
- Andrew Corbet (English cousin, Vevette's destined husband) arrives later.
- Vevette's daydream hero: "Lord Percy."

## Grange, Andrew, Grace's death (Ch. IV–VII)
- Ch. IV: Vevette's holiday; visits Lucille on rock above road; Lucille hates "the Religion." Procession of nuns to hospital; Lucille's brother's children taken from Gran'mère Luchon (old woman expelled from her cottage; new curé). Lucille's later disaffection. Father tells Vevette the secret: pastor Monsieur Bertheau to be hidden in old tower via secret passage from ruined chapel (stall, fourth seat, button). Lucille thought tampered with.
- Ch. V: Vevette at chapel at night with dog Hal (mastiff), receives pastor (countersign "The name of the Lord is a strong tower"/"To them that fear him"). Pastor dreams of daughter Angelique. Lucille (ch.V) apostatizes after kneeling to priest's Host procession, gives note; "Traitor"; wishes.
- Ch. VI: Andrew Corbet arrives (came with English ambassador's train). Andrew: short, broad, large nose, gray eyes, black hair. Loves Vevette from first hearing. Pastor's last Supper in grange vault; alarm of "horses" (escaped herd). Pastor drowned later in boat (sons of widow; one survived to Jersey).
- Ch. VII: Lucille's procession, Pierre Le Febre (wild Lucille-sweetheart, married Isabeau). Grace's sudden death; buried by night in vault under chapel (funeral service from mother's prayer-book). Andrew, father; "Mitspah" seal ring later.
- Ch. VIII: Secret passage to orchard ruin. Father's old friend Louis de Reviere (Capuchin friar, warned). Father goes to Avranches; killed by mob (Michaud, shot). Mob pillages Tour d'Antin; Michaud falls through floor. Blanchon the white cat (mute, growls/purrs) guards escape. Pierre Le Febre's boat to Jersey; Andrew, mother, Vevette escape.

## Jersey and England (Ch. IX–XI)
- Jersey: cousin Marianne Corbet (rector George Corbet's sister). Cousin George Corbet (rector, white curls). Girls: Katherine (elder), Paulina (second), Eleanor (nursing, gentle). Twin little boys. Vevette falls ill; recovers in spring.
- Pierre Le Febre goes to Jersey. Blanchon given to Eleanor.
- Ch. X: London. Uncle Charles (Corbet) and Aunt Jem (Jemima), court; Mr. Pepys (Samuel), Mrs. Pepys; jewels sold. Vevette presented to King Charles II. Aunt Jem's worldly ways; "Mr. Butler" bow scandal. Simon and Jeanne found at French church in Threadneedle Street.
- Ch. XI: Tre Madoc (Cornwall); Andrew's mother Aunt Amy; sister Betty (small, dark, mischievous), Margaret (tall, fair), Rosamond (studious, timid, Corbet bookish). Deborah Permuen (housekeeper). Well House with St. Wenna's well; fairy-like Dinah (foundling, gold dove pendant).

## Mischief and engagement breaks (Ch. XII–XIV)
- Betty's sabotage: Vevette's secret book (Dryden poems and play); Betty takes it, carries to Aunt Amy. Vevette rejects Andrew; Betty and Mr. Lovel (spendthrift, unbeliever) secret meetings at Torden's cottage; Lovel's accusation. Betty's marriage to Lovel; Mr. Dobson clergy blunder "What God hath put asunder...".
- Vevette moves to Well House with mother; Dinah as waiting gentlewoman; Simon and Jeanne. Andrew gives gold locket / Mitspah ring. Vevette teaches Lois Barker to read.
- Lord Stanton (cousin, Stanton Court, Devon) visits; mother's will makes him guardian. Mother dies suddenly at Stanton Court (Ch. XV).

## Stanton Court and London (Ch. XV–XVIII)
- Stanton Court: Lady Stanton (kind), Theo (Theodosia, pretty, later marries Dean of Exeter), Martha (cold, temper; married Captain Bernard), Lord Stanton's son Lewis (Lewis Stanton, handsome, wanted Vevette). Mr. Penrose (rector). Vevette runs Lady Rosamond's school with Dinah.
- Vevette drifts into worldliness; refuses Mr. Champernoun. Betty slanders her to Lady Stanton. Vevette leaves for London to Aunt Jem.
- London: Uncle Charles (gambler, debts), Aunt Jem (ill; dies). Mercer (maid, later schoolmistress in Hackney, refuses to go to Fayrolles). Monsieur and Madame de Fayrolles (Aunt Zenobie, rouged, Catholic; Vevette's paternal uncle the marquis Henri de Fayrolles). Father Martien (Jesuit, sharp).
- Vevette converts to Catholicism; sickness; becomes disillusioned. Monsieur de Luynes (ugly old suitor) refused; locked in garret; ugly gray cat companion.

## Canada plot and escape (Ch. XX–XXIII)
- Departs for Marseilles; sees Protestant Morin struck by Uncle Henri (de Fayrolles); Vevette defies him ("dastard").
- Meets foster-brother David at convent gate (Gospel of St. Luke; message to Lord Stanton / Andrew).
- Ursuline convent at Marseilles; Mother Superior, Mother Mary of the Incarnation (proud), Sister St. Stanislaus (kindly, mentions Lucille's drowning), Sister Joanne. Girls: Desirée (dies of scurvy), Louisonne (missing, later safe).
- Voyage to Canada on ship; storm; rescued by ship Good Hope (Captain Mayhew), bound for Boston. Andrew is captain's... (Andrew Corbet aboard as passenger/ship's man; "Captain Mayhew" name misused). Married on the spot by Mr. Norton (Church of England minister). Mother Mary angry.
- Boston: Mr. Folsom; Mrs. Folsom; Lucille found alive (escaped convent, works as interpreter). Andrew: Jamaica lady; Margaret married Mr. Treverthy; Betty in London.
- New England six years (farm near Hampton); Father Martien visits with Indians; return to Cornwall; three children. Aunt Amy receives them. Lucille with them; David in Penzance; Jeanne and Simon long lived.
- Final fates: Betty (no good word); Uncle Charles's Felicia; Monsieur de Fayrolles dies in duel; Aunt Zenobie to convent; Susanne; Lord Stanton; Lewis marries Provençal; Theo and Dean; Margaret with 20 children; Rosamond. Moral verses: James 1:8; 1 John 2:15; Matt 6:24. Signed "Agnes Genevieve Corbet née d'Antin."

# BOOK 2: The Crow's Inn Tragedy (Haynes, 1927 London mystery)

## Principal characters
- Luke Francis Bechcombe: senior solicitor, Bechcombe and Turner, Crow's Inn (corner house); widower? (no—husband of Madeline). Small, spare, grey, horn-rimmed spectacles, keeps money/records; murdered ~12 noon Feb 3 (per warrant) in his private office by strangulation after chloroform; body behind screen by window.
- Madeline Bechcombe (Mrs. Luke), Carlsford Square house; tall, dark-eyed, aquiline; hysterical; hates Mrs. Carnthwacke; sister of Rev. James Collyer's wife (Mrs. Collyer is Luke's wife's? — Collyer is Luke's brother-in-law: Mrs. Collyer, née Bechcombe, is Luke's sister).
- Rev. James Collyer: rector of Wexbridge; Luke's brother-in-law; gentle, pained; emeralds (Collyer cross) pawned to Luke; learns Aubrey was culprit; burns note; nervous breakdown.
- Anthony "Tony" Collyer: son of James; ex-soldier, D.S.O., gassed, prisoner in Germany; idle, debts; engaged to Cecily Hoyle; suspect.
- Aubrey Todmarsh: Tony's cousin (half-nephew of Luke, Mrs. Collyer's half-brother's son); head of St. Philip's Confraternity/Community at South London; conscientious objector; the Yellow Dog and actual murderer. Engaged to Mrs. Sadie Phillimore (American widow, actually a crook).
- Amos Thompson: managing clerk; embezzler; disappeared; actually Samuel Horsingforth alias John Frederick Hoyle, father of Cecily; lived Brooklyn Terrace room; arrested at Southampton on Atlantic.
- Cecily Frances Hoyle: secretary to Luke; gray coat, squirrel collar; Hobart Residence, Windover Square; claims Thompson adopted her; her "photograph" in Thompson's room.
- John Steadman: barrister, K.C.-type, Luke's cousin; sharp; conspicuous "Carnthwacke" examiner.
- Inspector William Furnival ("The Ferret") Scotland Yard; Dr. Hackett (doctor); Spencer, John Walls (clerks); Percy Johnson; Brunton (youth).
- Cyril B. Carnthwacke (American millionaire), Mrs. Carnthwacke (formerly Bella Laymond, stage actress), maid; Fédora (fortune teller).
- Mrs. Phillimore (Sadie), Madeline's guest; Butterfly; exposed as crook from Boston.
- Hopkins (Community man, arrested Whistone Hall burglary); wife's child rescued by Steadman.
- Lee Sweet (not in this book).
- Mr. Hoyle of Rose Cottage, Burford (alias Christopher Hoyle; housekeeper Mrs. Wye).
- Dr. J. Miles? no — that's Book 3.

## Plot events (key sequence)
1. Rev. James Collyer visits Luke's office; emeralds (Collyer cross) to be sold. Luke discovers they are paste. Tony mentioned as engaged to Cecily.
2. Aubrey's Community House, St. Philip's (South London); Michael Farmore arrested for burglary at General Craven's house.
3. Morning of murder: Mr. Pound and Mr. Geary clients. Tony shouted at Thompson, went to private door. Luke rings for Cecily ~11:45. Luke tells Cecily at 11:45. Cecily, Tony, to Field of Rest (St. Philip's churchyard). Luke recalls Tony to talk.
4. Thompson leaves ~12:30; Bank messenger waiting. Clerks break door ~2 p.m.; Luke dead behind screen; Dr. Hackett: died ~12. Clerk Spencer glimpsed leg.
5. Chloroform smell; rubber gloves; white glove (size too small for killer's hand) found by desk.
6. Mrs. Carnthwacke comes to office at 12:30 with diamonds; receipt signed Luke Francis Bechcombe, diamonds "deposited in safe" (cupboard, empty when opened). Later confesses she met impostor; face different; hands with long thumb, short forefinger.
7. Thompson found: Brooklyn Terrace, room; photograph of Cecily; library book (detective novels). Cecily's photograph found (Thompson's Brooklyn room). Telegram "Do not mention home address. Father." "Physical Energy" statue meeting.
8. Burford visit: Rose Cottage; Christopher Hoyle's fake signed sketches; Cecily's time-table with Burford underlined.
9. Mrs. Carnthwacke attacked (strangled with cord) in her car near Victoria Gate; survives (pretend dying); Carnthwacke hires inspector.
10. Thompson arrested at Southampton as Samuel Horsingforth (alias John Frederick Hoyle); Steadman and inspector.
11. Yellow Gang: Burlase Street, Limehouse; Golden Room; chairs trap; Steadman and inspector stripped, bound, pushed out window into river; escape by knife note; Yellow Dog revealed: Aubrey Todmarsh. Trap house burned.
12. Final: Aubrey arrested at Community house by inspector: "Aubrey William Todmarsh, alias the Yellow Dog," cyanide capsule replaced; Hopkins's wife helped escape. Tony and Cecily reconcile.

# BOOK 3: Cole of Spyglass Mountain (Hankins, 1923 western)

## Principal characters
- Joshua Cole (b. ~1906? age 14 at start; ~21 at pardon), gray-blue eyes, black hair; astronomer; ascetic face; sometimes "Tony" in House of Refuge ("Fifty-six thirty-five"); "Cole of Spyglass Mountain."
- Lester Cole: younger brother (~11–13), weakling who abandoned Joshua; later works in shoe store; Lester's birthday June 15 (21st) which triggers Joshua's inheritance.
- John Cole: father, traveling hardware salesman, cruel (duckings in bathtub), womanizer, gambler; dies? not stated; plotted with Slim.
- Blanche Florence Cole: mother, of aristocratic Maryland Florences; died (Joshua pardoned at ~20 after her death).
- Zida Hunt: negro cook/maid.
- Silvanus Madmallet: schoolteacher, "Ole Hothatchet," tyrannical; expelled Joshua for threatening with iron poker.
- Slinky Dawson: teacher's pet, carries note; "Did" Eustace; "Spud" Mulligan.
- Madge Mundy: "Shanty Madge," "Oriental-topaz eyes," frizzly bronze-gold hair, Pocahontas coloring; gypo queen; daughter of Bloodmop (George) Mundy (red hair, sky-blue eyes, died ~3 months before the story's events) and Elizabeth Mundy (dark hair; refined; aged 40+).
- Jawbone Mahoney: Irish boss-powderman who fired big shot drunk → tunnel slide ("Mundy slide").
- Philip Demarest (contractor; blue eyes, white beard), Spruce, Tillou (Demarest, Spruce and Tillou: main contractors).
- Bluenose: Joshua's fellow powderman/hammerman.
- Jack Montgomery: wealthy suitor; Montgomery and Applegate contractors; later Madge's fiancé. Sister Mary Montgomery.
- California Bill Fox: freighter (six-mule), ex-deputy sheriff, slate-gray eyes, shrewd; "character"; "hi-yu skookum."
- Felix Wolfgang ("Slim Wolfgang"): Number Twenty-three forty-four at House of Refuge; gambler; freckled; billiard-top vest; shot Joshua with thirty-thirty; plotted to keep Joshua out of East for inheritance. Girl: Winnie the Weeper.
- The Whimperer (Chicago-born panhandler/John Yegg; artificial scar, twisted face; stole telescope, sold $100; later confessed).
- Beaver Clegg: House of Refuge Juvenile Dept head; ugly/lincoln-like; astronomer (variable star observer; 3-inch refractor); died of heart failure; willed telescope.
- Lee Sweet: cattleman (Box-R Ranch), drunk, bearded; harasses homesteaders; shoots at Joshua's cabin.
- Dr. J. Miles Stanhope: Ragtown medic; Van Dyke beard; roulette; Gladys.
- Dickinson: plainclothes detective; Peter Henry Florence: Joshua's maternal uncle (Virginian), founded House of Refuge.

## Events in order
1. Spring, Hathaway (city): Joshua (14, Cole) and brother Lester skip school; Joshua threatens teacher Silvanus Madmallet with poker; expelled. Slug experiment on chip and razor.
2. Father John Cole intends to duck him; Joshua flees; meets Madge at Crescent Skating Rink; asks to skate; Madge's gypo family (mother Elizabeth, father Bloodmop) in camp on railroad grade.
3. Joshua goes to gypo camp; Bloodmop hires him as driver; Madge teaches stars; Joshua and Madge talk astronomy under stars ("Big Dipper steamer chair").
4. Detective Dickinson arrests Joshua; father swears warrant; House of Refuge commitment (Juvenile Department of Beaver Clegg). Father's threat.
5. Clegg takes him to roof at night; moon through telescope; teaches astronomy; Joshua deliberately starts fight to avoid parole (pardoned 6 years later at 20). T-and-H medal.
6. Clegg dies; Joshua inherits telescope/books; Lester keeps papers.
7. Tramp life, The Whimperer (jocker) who steals telescope; Joshua at Ragtown (roadside skeleton game; Slim Wolfgang chase); Joshua stays in camp, slug epiphany (“Man the slug”).
8. Spur: Joshua hired by Demarest, Spruce and Tillou on Gold Belt Cut-off; California Bill Fox (freighter).
9. Madge is shanty queen of Mundy outfit; Hill of Springs tunnel with mud springs.
10. Joshua goes to Camp One; Spyglass Mountain mentioned; homestead claim filed (Los Angeles land office); buys gray Argo (dapple gray) and saddle.
11. Ragtown: Slim Wolfgang runs stud at Golden Eagle; Lee Sweet confrontation; Winnie the Weeper.
12. Jawbone's shot → tunnel slide; Joshua proposes coyote hole plan (drawing); Demarest accepts; slide stopped; $5000 reward refused by Joshua. Joshua shot by Slim's rifle before proposal (rifle at close range from Slim's tent). Madge: "Hercules and the firebrand."
13. Madge and mother abandon mining, move to homestead; Joshua builds cabin, observatory, telescope on Spyglass Mountain; writes articles (Universe, American Astronomer, Journal of Astronomy) "Cole of Spyglass Mountain."
14. Madge goes to LA; Jack Montgomery engagement; letter ("Please forget me").
15. Lee Sweet fires at Joshua's cabin; burns; Slim/Winnie plot to bump Joshua; The Whimperer confessions.
16. June 15/18: Joshua at observatory; Mars configuration observed ~12:10 a.m. June 18; Sweet's rifle fire; Joshua shot off ladder (unconscious; camera left).
17. California Bill confronts Slim and Winnie in tent (bluffs with .32 automatic, clasps Slim's wrist); Slim confesses: Uncle Peter Henry Florence's will leaves Joshua $150,000 at 21; Lester inherits if Joshua dies; father John Cole hired Slim; Slim's plot.
18. Joshua reinterpret; Madge returns; Joshua lies in hospital at Ragtown; telegram to Milton University; Dr. Emanuel Schlott (German) confirms configuration (photographed); Joshua vindicated ("Cole of Spyglass Mountain famous in a night"). Madge says "I've come back to Spyglass Mountain!" Final scene: newspaper; Madge and Joshua embrace.

Key quoted lines: "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain!"; "A dreamer lives forever, and a toiler dies in a day" (John Boyle O'Reilly poem); "Thus was she subdued!" (Madge); "Cole of Spyglass Mountain" (California Bill's name).
